Why one a day

Most detailers book three cars a day. I book one.

Plenty of places advertise a full detail in ninety minutes. I genuinely can't see how that works — cleaning a boot properly can take an hour on its own.

So I only take one vehicle a day. That means no clock-watching, no cutting the polish short because there's another car waiting on the drive, and no dragging yesterday's grit across your paint with a tired wash mitt.

It also means I have to charge more than the hand wash down the road. That's the trade, and I'd rather be upfront about it than pretend otherwise.

  • Fresh microfibres and regularly replaced mitts on every car
  • Non-acidic wheel cleaner — safe on every finish
  • Premium products, whether it's a Kia Rio or a Bugatti
  • Honest advice when a cheaper option is the right one

The process

Six stages. Every single car.

Every stage, every car. This is what separates a detail from a wash.

01Step 1

Decontaminate

Citrus pre-wash, snow foam and a full chemical decontamination — iron fallout and tar dissolved off the paint rather than rubbed off it. Nothing gets touched until the grit is gone — that's what causes swirl marks.

02Step 2

Wash safely

Two buckets, fresh microfibre mitts, non-acidic wheel cleaner. Every panel by hand.

03Step 3

Correct

Machine polish where the paint needs it. 70–80% of swirls and light scratches, cut out properly.

04Step 4

Deep clean inside

Extraction, steam and sanitisation. Vents, seams, stitch lines, panel gaps — fine-pick detailing throughout.

05Step 5

Protect

Ceramic sealant, wax or a multi-year coating. Glass treated, trims conditioned, tyres dressed.

06Step 6

Aftercare

Advice on keeping it that way — and why an automated wash undoes the work fastest. A two-bucket hand wash and a plush drying towel is all it takes.

Before you book

The questions I get asked most.

Why are you more expensive than my local car wash?

Because a cheap car wash is the single biggest cause of swirl marks and scratches in paintwork. The same brushes and the same dirty mitts go over every car, dragging the last customer's grit across yours.

I use fresh microfibres, regularly replaced brushes and mitts, and quality products on every car regardless of whether it's a Kia Rio or a Bugatti. Your local wash may well be cheaper today. The scratches it leaves behind cost far more to correct later than the difference you saved.

How does booking a day work?

I only ever take one vehicle a day, so the day is yours — your car isn't sharing my time with anyone else's.

When I confirm your booking I'll give you a realistic idea of what to expect so you can plan around it. I'd always rather be straight with you upfront than rush the job to hit a slot.

Do you need parking, water and electricity?

Yes — a parking space next to the vehicle, an outside tap and a plug point.

The space matters as much as the water. Everything I use travels with me, so it all has to sit within reach of the car while I work, and I need your outside tap to run the wash. I carry 30 metres of hose and extension lead, so anywhere within that distance of the house is fine.

If any of that is a problem, say so when you enquire — there's usually a way around it and I'd much rather sort it out beforehand than turn up and find we're stuck.

Are you insured?

Yes, fully insured. I'm happy to provide the documents as proof if you'd like to see them before booking.
